/repos/lumen-fx/lumen/issues/562.body:
The crash tests flaked on macOS: one run got the in-process report with "the crash helper was not running", another had the child give up waiting for the helper. Both came from the same gap. On macOS minidumper binds the helper's socket before it checks in the Mach port dump requests use, so an app connecting in between sees the connect succeed and the port lookup fail, closes, and retries. The helper took that first closed connection for the app leaving and exited. Depending on timing the retry then found no helper at all, or finished the handshake against the closing socket and counted the helper as up.

The helper now exits on zero clients only after the app has said hello; an app that dies before connecting is still caught by the existing watch on its process. The app counts the helper as up only once a ping is answered, so a handshake against a dead socket no longer passes. A new case closes a connection without a hello and checks the helper stays, and the test now carries the child's stderr into every exit assertion.

Two Linux races in the same suite surfaced under load and are fixed here too: the helper wrote the report in place, so a reader could see it half written, and it now writes a hidden file and renames it; and a copied test executable could fail with ETXTBSY while a child forked from another test thread still held its write descriptor, so the copy and the spawns are serialized.

The os/crash tests passed 20 of 20 idle and 40 of 40 with every core busy on Linux; before the last two fixes the loaded runs failed with ETXTBSY and with a truncated report. Three `workflow_dispatch` CI runs of the branch (39664982434, 39671224351, 39681485471) passed the crash tests on macOS, Linux and Windows. fmt and clippy with `-D warnings` are clean.

Closes #557
Closes #559
Closes #560

commit.message:
fix(crash): keep the helper up when a connection closes before its hello

On macOS the helper's socket listens a moment before minidumper registers
the Mach port dumps travel on. An app that connects in that moment finds
no port, closes the connection and tries again, and the helper read that
close as its last client leaving and exited. The app then either never
reached it, or completed a handshake against the closing socket, counted
the helper as up, and wrote the in-process report when the dump request
found no port.

The helper now ends on its last disconnect only once the app has said
hello; the watch thread still ends it if the app dies first. The app
counts the helper as up only after it answers a ping. The end-to-end
test keeps the crashing child's stderr for its failure messages, and a
new case closes a connection unannounced and checks the helper stays.

Closes #557

fix(crash): write the report through a hidden file

The report was written in place, so anyone opening it while the helper
was still writing (the crash tests, or a person in the crash folder) got
it cut short. It is now written to a hidden file and renamed into place.

Closes #560

test(crash): start processes apart from writing executables

The tests run on threads of one process. A child forked from one thread
holds the write descriptor of an executable another thread is copying
until it execs, and Linux then refuses to run the copy. Copying and
starting processes now take one lock.

Closes #559
